history.dynasty: Habshi (Abyssinian) dynasty of the Bengal Sultanate
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Firoz Minar is a five-storeyed Indo-Islamic victory tower at Gaur (not Malda city; ~16 km south of Malda town), built by Sultan Saifuddin Firuz Shah of the Habshi dynasty between 1485 and 1489, reportedly to commemorate his battlefield victories. The 26 m tower, in Tughlaqi style with terracotta ornamentation, resembles the Qutb Minar of Delhi: its first three storeys are dodecagonal and the upper two circular, with a 73-step spiral staircase inside. The dome that once crowned it was replaced by a flat roof during restoration. It stands about 1 km from the Dakhil Darwaza and is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. Tradition holds that the Sultan had the chief architect Piru thrown from the top for boasting he could have built it taller. Latitude/longitude from the published site coordinates; the map geocoder returned a conflicting, misplaced English Bazar POI, so coordinates should be treated as sourced from Wikipedia/ASI data.

name: Firoz Minar
town_description: Gaur (Gour), in Malda district near the Bangladesh border, was the medieval capital of Bengal for several centuries and is now a scattered field of ruins - mosques, gateways and towers - protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. It lies about 16 km from Malda town (English Bazar) and is reached by a road passing the Dakhil Darwaza. The nearest functional airport is Bagdogra, ~224 km away, and the town of Malda is a major railway junction.

travel.airport: Bagdogra Airport (IXB), ~224 km; Malda Airport is non-operational
travel.road: Malda-Gaur road from Malda town, ~16 km; ~330 km from Kolkata via NH 12

visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily 7:00 AM - 6:00 PM (Saturday 7:00 AM - 4:40 PM); interior staircase usually closed to visitors
